correctness.rationale: On locally finite leafless rooted T, the map f↦(f(o),Δf) is an isometric identification of big/little Lipschitz norms with C ⊕ ℓ∞(E) and C ⊕ c0(E). Parent composition acts as 1⊕D where Dg=0 in depth one and g(parent) otherwise. Leaflessness makes D an isometry, so for |λ|<1, ||(D-λ)g||≥(1-|λ|)||g||, giving injectivity and closed range; |λ|>1 is invertible by Neumann. If only finitely many branching vertices, stripping a finite head leaves k=1+∑(d-1) unilateral shifts, each Fredholm index -1 for |λ|<1. With infinite branching, for each u choose disjoint child rays and define L_u(g)=∑_{j>=0} λ^j(g(a_j)-g(b_j)); absolutely convergent and annihilates D-λ. The functionals are independent by choosing a minimum-depth branching vertex among a finite relation, giving infinite cokernel. Unit-circle tent vectors λ^{-depth}h_depth have norm one and residual ≤1/N and lie in c0 and ℓ∞, so injective D-λ cannot be Fredholm there. Polynomial result follows from Calkin invertibility and index additivity. The proof is genuinely infinite-dimensional; toy rank checks cannot replace it. Spectrum is the closed disk, with scalar eigenvalue 1 already contained.
residual_risks: No independent formal Banach-space implementation; the Fredholm argument was checked algebraically, including c0 finite-support and ℓ∞ closed-range points.
